QUESTION OF THE WEEK - Economists were asked for preliminary forecasts of third quarter CPI and underlying inflation. While the forecasts will be fine tuned between now and when the data is released on October 23, initial forecasts show economists expect both measures to be below the increases of the June quarter, which were 0.6 percent for the headline rate and 0.8 percent for the underlying.
In annual terms the forecasts work through to annual rates of 2.3 percent for the headline rate and 2.5 percent for the underlying rate.

The reduction in interest rates announced for competition reasons by the banks in June will affect the headline rate this quarter. However, the impact of the cuts following the July 31 cut in official interest rates will be seen more in the December quarter as the cuts were effective from mid-September.

For the underlying rate, the median forecast implies an annualised rate in the middle of the two to three percent target range. Annualising the June and September quarters, however, would produce a figure of 2.8 percent, at the high end of the target range.

An underlying figure of 0.5 percent or lower, which would lead to a year-to increase of less than 2.5 percent, would probably be needed to justify another rate cut on the grounds of an improvement in the inflation outlook, economists said.

MERCHANDISE IMPORTS - Economists said that although the underlying in trend in imports was soft, a number of factors were pointing to an increase in August. Imports have fallen by in each of the last three months, to be down a total of 8.0 percent, and so are due for a rebound; capital good imports have fallen by a total of 22.7 percent over the last two months and given the strong business investment expectations should show either a flattening out or a rise; the Australian dollar was softer in the month; and finally, many economists expect the data to include an aircraft import worth about A$100 million.
